Antique Bibles range from under **$100** for individual antique leaves, pocket editions, and modern facsimiles up to **$25,000+** for rare 16th- and 17th-century editions and illustrated folios.[[1]](https://thebiblemuseum.com/)[[2]](https://moons-rare-books.myshopify.com/collections/bibles-automated)[[3]](https://www.baumanrarebooks.com/rare-books/religion/bibles/)

### Notable Listings & Price Ranges

- **Single Antique Leaves & Reprints ($18–$175):** Individual original leaves—such as a 1613 King James "He" leaf from [Historic Bibles & Engravings](https://historicbibles.com/product/king-james-1613-he-numbers-6-7/?srsltid=AYCX9vIXbrzQf5FWkCszKEXXnucjYcXkC6reJk-Fyqk7Uw-DpKZitMDduN0) ($175) or a 1640 Geneva leaf ($18)—as well as complete facsimiles like a 1611 King James reprint from [Kingdomwear](https://www.kingdomwear.com/products/1611-king-james-bible-brown?variant=46742377922780&country=US&currency=USD&utm_medium=product_sync&utm_source=google&utm_content=sag_organic&utm_campaign=sag_organic&srsltid=AYCX9vLSMfK7DTm0kvN5uuFQWwkHKIT2uPgBMU1TUKouTEDesPDTXpbReFc) ($59.95).[[1]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:13202456090997646763&ibp=oshop)[[2]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:4781446591254191003&ibp=oshop)[[3]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:11510165578832896212&ibp=oshop)
- **19th-Century & Pocket Bibles ($80–$350):** Leather-bound Victorian, family, and pocket editions, including a [1901 New Testament and Psalms](https://vintagebookworms.com/products/1901-new-testament-and-psalms-antique-87316) from [Vintage Bookworms](https://vintagebookworms.com/products/1901-new-testament-and-psalms-antique-87316) ($82.45) and various 1850–1899 editions on [eBay](https://www.ebay.com/b/Bible-Books-1850-1899/29223/bn_55466751) ($70–$350+).[[1]](https://www.ebay.com/b/Bible-Books-1850-1899/29223/bn_55466751)[[2]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:14649716163593200161&ibp=oshop)
- **17th-Century Editions ($4,500–$25,000):** Scarce early printings and folios, such as a [1614/1615 Early Quarto King James Bible](https://www.antiquebible.com/shop/p/1614/1615-early-quarto-king-james-bible-with-genealogies-and-map?srsltid=AYCX9vJvKIQjkJY_Ujyl-veDV6onWKXn8eOc2JusPrbC_MMekSU5NeQtt5c) from [Antique Bible](https://www.antiquebible.com/shop/p/1614/1615-early-quarto-king-james-bible-with-genealogies-and-map?srsltid=AYCX9vJvKIQjkJY_Ujyl-veDV6onWKXn8eOc2JusPrbC_MMekSU5NeQtt5c) ($4,500), a [1634 Folio King James Bible](https://www.patricksrarebooks.com/product-page/king-james-bible-1634-folio-the-fourth-59-line-bible) from [Patrick's Rare Books](https://www.patricksrarebooks.com/product-page/king-james-bible-1634-folio-the-fourth-59-line-bible) ($15,000), and a [1660 John Field Restoration Bible](https://www.antiquebible.com/shop/p/1660-john-fields-restoration-bible-with-80-double-engraved-plates?srsltid=AYCX9vJymDK7thQHkF8ZhoCv3MFxhyFfR2vHfaYKAEfSzIr-xDDJVKY7L30) ($25,000).[[1]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:4583367483798811658&ibp=oshop)[[2]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:6956047794575422030&ibp=oshop)[[3]](https://www.google.com/search?q=product&prds=pvt:hg,pvo:29,productid:16304629249870914372&ibp=oshop)

### Specialist Dealers & Catalogs

- [Antique Bible](https://www.antiquebible.com/shop) — Carries 16th- and 17th-century King James , Geneva, and Great Bible editions.[[1]](https://www.antiquebible.com/shop)
- [Bauman Rare Books](https://www.baumanrarebooks.com/rare-books/religion/bibles/) — Offers rare Bibles, Books of Common Prayer, and early translations ($4,800–$25,000+).[[1]](https://www.baumanrarebooks.com/rare-books/religion/bibles/)
- [TheBibleMuseum.com](https://thebiblemuseum.com/) — Features antique Bibles, facsimiles, and original leaves spanning the 16th to 19th centuries ($49–$8,500).[[1]](https://thebiblemuseum.com/)
- [Moons Rare Books](https://moons-rare-books.myshopify.com/collections/bibles-automated) — Stocks original leaves, replicas, polyglots, and antique editions ($74.99–$15,000).[[1]](https://moons-rare-books.myshopify.com/collections/bibles-automated)

To narrow down the best options, let me know:

- **How you plan to use it** (collecting/investment, display, family history, or reading)
- **Your budget** and **preferred era or translation** (such as 16th–17th century Geneva or King James vs. 19th-century family Bibles)
- Whether you want a **complete book** , a **single leaf** , or a **facsimile**

references.title: King James - 1613 HE - NUMBERS 6-7
references.text: NUMBERS 6:19-7:78. "Aaronic Blessing" (6:24-27). King James "He" Bible. Printed in London by Robert Barker, 1613. First Quarto Black Letter Edition. Overall size: 8.6" x 6.25". Reference: Herbert 323 (text block 199mm x 138mm), the "He" edition, containing the original error in Ruth 3:15 "he went into the citie" and according to Herbert a "close reprint" of the 1611 folio "He" first edition, first issue. This 1613 "He" edition is the second and also the last of its kind; after 1613, no other "He" editions were printed. Note: There are no other certain determinations of a "He" edition than the Ruth 3:15 citation and the block size, since textual indicators vary and are somewhat mixed, despite what some experts may say. The best indicator of a genuine 1613 "He" Bible, therefore, is the correct block size and the Ruth 3:15 citation together, in an original Bible that also appears to be original in all its parts, that is, with uniform pages throughout. Such a bible is the represented here, from which these leaves were taken. For scholarly reference, see Herbert's Historical Catalogue of English Bibles. This leaf cites the ancient and profoundly theological Aaronic Blessing. The leaf is in EXCELLENT condition; light smudges to inner margin (see pics). COA (with corrected verses) on premium "gold leaf" paper with signature and gold seal. This leaf sets in a museum quality Bi-fold Portfolio. Call for specific leaf requests.

Genuine first edition reprint in its entirety of the 1611 King James Bible, including but not limited to: -BIBLE MEASURES 11" x 7" x 1.5" and weighs 3 lbs. with smythe-sewn binding printed on 35g white Bible paper - original 1611 title page - original OT and NT title pages - original translators to King James dedication - original translators to the reader letter - original calendar - original table of contents page - original lion and unicorn crest page - original genealogies of Holy Scriptures and Jesus Christ - original Jerusalem and holy land map - original Gothic font (black letter font) - original spellings - original rubrication - original art work - original 39 OT books - original 14 Apocrypha books - original 27 NT books - all faux leather soft cover brown - deep embossing front and side cover - saddle stitch cover - 3 x place holder ribbons - gold gilded paper edges - extra high grade bible paper - light weight for easy carry - durable construction for strong use

references.title: King James Bible, 1634 folio, the fourth 59-line Bible
references.text: The Holy bible, Containing the Old Testament, and the New: Newly Translated out of the Originall Tongues: And with the former Translations diligently compared and reuised, By his Maiesties speciall Commandment. Appointed to be read in Churches. Imprinted at London by Robert Barker, Printer to the Kings most Excellent Maiestie: and by the Assignes of Iohn bill. Anno Dom. 1634. Cum Privilegio. New Testament title page reads “The Newe Testament of our Lord and Sauiour Iesvs Christ. Newly Translated out of the Originall Greeke:” [and thereafter same as the general title page]. General and New Testament engraved tile pages present. Decorative capitals, head & tail pieces. Prelims in red and black. Set in two columns of 59 lines. Black letter. Folio in early (original?) full brown leather over boards. Blind stamped. Raised bands on spine. Several areas of scratching and scuffing, particularly on rear board. Tears and losses of leather at head and tail of spine, and along middle of front joint. Peeling near bottom of front joint. Hinges cracked. Joints secure. Lacking 6D5 & 6D6 (final two leaves of Revelation). Ffep and general title page attached but coming loose. Ffep with folds. Prior owner’s inscriptions and names (Wheeler family) on front paste down (prescription for whooping cough) and verso of title page (with a birth and death note of 1804 – 1809). Vertical closed tears to gutter D1 (prelim), and 3M4. 5K6-6A5 with frayed leaves and damp stain. Vertical tear near tail of gutter progressing gradually from 5I6 – 6A5, slightly involving marginal text. Many corners with creases, and a few thumbed with losses just barely into the Biblical text. Scattered worming and damp stains, mostly in prelims and epistles through Apocalypse—most of the Biblical leaves are fresh and bright. End papers tattered and creased. Ffep, A-B⁴, C⁶, A – Cccccc⁶, Dddddd⁴, rfep. Darlow & Moule 376 “the fourth distinct folio edition printed in large black-letter, of King James’6 version.” Herbert 487. Signatures as in 1617 edition. New Royal Arms with copyright preceding dedication. D1b = “These to bee observed.” D4a = “To finde Easter for ever.” Heb xii:1 = “runne with patience the race” instead of “unto the race.” A 59-line King James Bible, following the 1617, 1613, and 1611 respectively. A smaller font 72-line edition was also issued in 1617.

references.title: 1660 John Field’s Restoration Bible with 80 Double Engraved Plates
references.text: The Holy Bible containing the Bookes of the Old and New Testament... Summary A pulpit folio Field’s Bible commemorating the restoration of Charles II. Bound in brown morocco with eighty double plate engravings including the very large foldout of Jerusalem. Description 2 vols. Engraved title page (1660) by Diepenbeeck and Lambart featuring King Solomon on the throne with David, Moses, and Aaron above. Double page plate of Adam and Eve in the Garden featuring a variety of animals including a unicorn. Text in two column Roman font. Bound with a total of 80 double-page engravings by Visscher which include maps by Hollar, a large fold-out of Jerusalem, and various biblical scenes. Fifty-one engravings in the Old Testament which includes the Apocrypha. Printed New Testament title page (1659) with 29 engravings. Ends on printed colophon (1659). Collation [par]⁴, [par][par]⁴, A-Z⁶, Aa-Zz⁶, Aaa-Vvv⁶, Xxx⁴ (Genesis-Proverbs); Xxx5,6, Yyy-Zzz⁶, Aaaa-Yyyy⁶, Zzzz⁸, a-y⁴, A-Z⁶, Aa-Dd⁶, Ee⁸ (Ecclesiastes – Revelation). Complete with all title pages. Binding Rebacked in brown morocco. Original boards with gilt paneled border. Spines with girl tooling to recessed bands and compartments. Each spine with red morocco labels and the words “Holy Bible” and volume number lettered in gilt. Marbled endpapers. All edges marbled. Condition The text is clean and bright with wide margins throughout; title page trimmed to edges and laid down; Zz4 with small burnhole to margin; a handful of engravings with marginal closed tears. Note A very good copy of the popular Restoration Bible celebrating the return of Charles II. The text was first published the previous year by John Field, printer to the University of Cambridge, who had been commissioned to supply a lectern bible for use in churches and libraries. Former university Vice-Chancellor John Worthington noted that “For a fair large letter, large paper, with fair margin ... there was never such a Bible in being”. This work is the first King James Bible provided with illustrations, and with 80 beautiful double-plate engravings. References Herbert 668; ESTC R17044; Wing B2258.
